sentences.text: The petitioners herein are accused Nos.1 to 8 in the above case.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel appearing for the de facto complainant and the injured persons and the learned Public Prosecutor.
3. In this matter, offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 324 and 448 read with Section 149 of IPC are alleged to have been committed by the accused.

4. It is submitted that the matter has been amicably settled and the de facto complainant and the injured persons CRL.MC NO. 2594 OF 2024 filed separate affidavits in this regard in a case involving matrimonial dispute.
Complainant is none other than the wife of the 1st accused.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor also submitted that the matter has been settled between the parties and statements of the de facto complainant and two other injured persons, viz., Sulojanaangath and Prasobh to that effect have been recorded.

6. Since the dispute has been settled in between husband and wife and her relatives, there is no reason to disallow the prayer for quashment, so as to facilitate peaceful living of the married couple.
Moreover, the dispute between the petitioners and the complainant is purely personal in nature and no public interest is involved.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, I am inclined to allow this petition.

In the result, this petition stands allowed and Annexure A2 Final Report and all further proceedings in C.C.No.709/2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class CRL.MC NO. 2594 OF 2024 Magistrate Court, Malappuram, arose out of Crime No.231/2022 of Kondotty Police Station, Malappuram,
stand quashed.
